decks.name: Sea Areas
decks.world: Radio 4 long wave, 198 kHz, 00:48: the Shipping Forecast read in order of the sea areas over a lighthouse whose Fresnel beam sweeps the fog twice every ten seconds. The light is that beam, white through grey, with port red and starboard green at the edges and Admiralty chart buff underneath; the sea is a wireframe swell that never breaks. There is no monster here, only weather, and the wonder is order spoken calmly into darkness for strangers who cannot see the person speaking. Register: Met Office cadence, gale warnings, pressure falling slowly, good occasionally poor, 1970s continuity-announcer vowels.

palette.why: water at midnight, green-black, never blue
the bed itself; the only deck whose environment is lighter than its figure
Fresnel white through fog; the strobe and the scope and nothing else
harbour red at the left edge of the aura, desaturated so it is a lamp, not a gel
harbour green at the right edge; together they say which way the frame is sailing
Admiralty chart buff for the swell wireframe and every word of the forecast

layer_notes.1: Abstract Field Smoke Storm in fog grey, low contrast, drifting left: the fog over water; Sailing By uses a Gradient horizon with the line in the lower third.
layer_notes.2: Line Scape as the swell, wireframe in chart buff, amplitude on the bass band with a slow release; Dogger Fisher swaps to Lines horizontal as the chart's latitude ruling.
layer_notes.3: Shaper tall thin rectangle as the lighthouse silhouette, never lit itself; Rings as the beam's bands in The Beam; a single Shaper triangle for Rockall.
layer_notes.4: Shaper white wedge rotating once per ten seconds, blurred, the Fresnel beam; Stroboscope programmed to the character Fl(2) 10s, two flashes then dark.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator, one sea area or one forecast phrase per scene, chart buff, lower-left like a chart legend; Falling Slowly uses Text Block for the four-line forecast.
layer_notes.6: Gradient horizontal port red to starboard green at 8 percent, the harbour lights; chart scenes swap to Solid Color chart buff Multiply.
layer_notes.7: Static fine as long-wave crackle at 8 percent plus Lines soft horizontal at 5 percent as rain; no film grain in this deck.
layer_notes.8: Sine Wave FFT trace in beam white, bottom quarter, same geometry as every deck.

moments: The beam: in scene 6 the row-4 wedge rotates once every ten seconds with the Radar button lit; roll the bank-B knob up so Wave Warp pushes the fog as the beam passes, and keep fader 3 at half so the lighthouse stays a silhouette.

The litany: scenes 3 and 4 put one sea-area name on row 5 per column; walk Up and Down slowly in the forecast's cadence rather than the beat, and let the Line Scape swell on row 2 ride the bass alone.

Rockall: walk Down to scene 8, drop faders 2 and 4, leave the single rock on row 3, the fog Bed and the Scope, and let the Vignette close with the master fader so the set ends on one shape in grey light.

effect_wishlist.role: persistence: the stacked pulsar plot, the moth's path in smoke, the beam's afterglow
phosphor curvature and scanline for the Dish and the Cosmonaut; the period lens
the lamp's throw; every deck darkens at the edges and the master fader closes it
candle, beam, blade glint; the only glow allowed
the chart recorder's step and the 16 fps projector; makes smooth generators look mechanical
1-bit line-printer quantise for Arecibo and terminal text
three-strip dye reduction; collapses gradients into gel
Technicolor misregistration; Giallo only, on the flash only
the lighthouse sweep and the dish scan; a rotating wipe with a period
the seance table's symmetry; folds static into faces
heat on reentry, fog pushed by the beam, water under the swell
the heartbeat stops; hold the frame on the breakdown
horizontal lens streak on the strobe; Carpenter's flare
single-hue grade per deck when the Aura layer is not enough

proposals.fft_philosophy: Sub and low (the kick) drive only impulse parameters with fast attack and slow release: Stroboscope trigger probability, Stop Motion step, the knock, the Metaball swell. Low-mids (the bass line) drive the amplitude of structural generators (Line Scape height, Pulsar ridge, Tunnelines speed, Smoke Storm turbulence) smoothed over about 300 ms so the room breathes rather than jumps. Highs (hats, air) drive texture only: Static opacity, Bloom threshold, Flicker Reel intensity, never position or scale. A long RMS envelope over several seconds drives Aura opacity and Vignette width so builds open the room and breakdowns close it. Nothing follows the raw signal, and these never react at all: text position, size or opacity (words are read, not shaken), hue or gel colour (the period is the colour and it does not flash), the Scope's own gain (it is the honest readout), the Bed layer's scale and position (the environment does not dance), and scene changes.
proposals.wildcard_rationale: Sea Areas belongs beside Space and Halloween because all five rooms make the same gesture: a signal sent into darkness toward someone who cannot see you. The Dish listens, the Cosmonaut transmits, Giallo and the Seance ask; the Shipping Forecast is the one that answers, order read into fog at 00:48 for strangers on water, with a lighthouse that is literally a Stroboscope with a published character. It is the same hardware and period as the performer's EarthSearch world (long wave, valve radio, BBC continuity), and its found language (good occasionally poor, falling slowly, rough or very rough) cuts into grammar rows as cleanly as Lexicon's ad-breaks. It is also the only deck with a horizon and a dawn, which gives a night of red and black somewhere to land.

proposals.tagline: Five rooms where someone is listening for something that may not answer: a dish, a séance, a lamp, a ten-day exposure, and a voice counting in the static.

decks.name: Big Ear
decks.world: The Ohio State Big Ear and the Jodrell Bank Lovell dish, 1967 to 1977: a wire-mesh reflector turning against a sky that is pure noise until, once a decade, it isn't. Light here is chart-recorder ink on fan-fold paper, phosphor on a Tektronix, and the sodium lamps of a car park at 3am. The wonder is clerical: a graduate student with a ruler finds the first pulsar in 400 feet of paper, and a volunteer writes Wow! in a margin. Cold, exact, monochrome with one amber, and the beat belongs to a dead star.

palette.why: near-black with a trace of blue: the sky as a receiver sees it, not black but cold
the ridgeline ink; cold paper white so the pulsar plot reads from the back of the room
ice blue for the dish rings and the feed horn; the 1420 MHz hydrogen line gets a colour nothing else gets
pure white only for the pulsar strobe; nothing else in this deck is allowed to be fully white
amber telemetry, the one warm thing: the chart-recorder margin note
a deep blue wash the rest of the deck sits in; the only colour field, never above 40 percent

layer_notes.1: Abstract Field 'Dot Dot Dot' at very low density drifting at glacial speed: the sky survey, a few hundred faint points; in No Carrier it becomes Static at full density because the signal is gone.
layer_notes.2: React Pulsar is the spine of the deck, the CP1919 stacked ridgeline with row count and amplitude on the smoothed low band; columns 1 to 3 swap it for Line Scape (the dish surface as wire mesh) and Sine Wave (the pen trace).
layer_notes.3: Rings: the dish beam pattern and the pulsar's own lighthouse cone, centred and slowly expanding; Shaper gives a single thin hexagon for the feed horn; Spiral in Dawn Chorus for the spectrogram curl.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope at the real pulsar period, one white flash every 1.337 seconds, hard and short; Wow Signal swaps it for a slow white Gradient bloom that rises and falls over 72 seconds like the original signal.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator telemetry in amber, fixed centre-low like a chart margin: coordinates, frequencies, the 6EQUJ5 string; nothing animates except the typewriter reveal.
layer_notes.6: Gradient radial, deep blue to black, breathing over about 8 seconds; Dawn Chorus crossfades it to a pale pre-dawn blue-grey.
layer_notes.7: Static, fine and low: receiver noise; in No Carrier it goes coarse and bright and becomes the whole picture.
layer_notes.8: Sine Wave oscilloscope of the live FFT, cold green, thin line, bottom quarter of frame; identical in every deck.

moments: Fire Scene Launch 5 (Pulsar Lock) and hold the row-4 LIGHT pad so the 1.337-second strobe runs under the ridgeline, then open the Trails bank knob to about half and watch each flash leave a ghost that decays exactly on the next pulse.

In Wow Signal, tap the row-5 TEXT pad on the beat to retrigger the 6EQUJ5 typewriter while the row-2 pulsar body is up, and on the drop hit Invert RGB for one bar so the paper goes black and the ink goes white.
Walk Down from Wow Signal into No Carrier for the breakdown so everything but the Static grain and the scope drops out, then ride the Vignette knob fully shut and back open as Dawn Chorus lands.

decks.name: Red Room
decks.world: A 1972 séance in a Turin apartment shot by a Giallo cinematographer: Art Nouveau wallpaper, venetian blinds, three candles, five sitters, an upturned glass, and a J&B bottle just out of frame. Light is candle amber and a red that is not blood but a Technicolor print of blood, with one cold spot that opens in the room when something answers. The dread is procedural: a knock, a tilt, a letter at a time. Hammer gold, Argento red, Victorian spiritualist manners, and nothing is ever shown.

palette.why: oxblood black: the room with the lights off, warm, never neutral grey
Profondo red for the wallpaper and the blinds; a print red, slightly orange, never pure #ff0000
candle gold for the glass, the planchette and the ring of hands; Hammer's gilt
candle-flame white, warm, the only thing allowed to flicker
parchment: a typed sitting record, so the words read as evidence not as titles
the cold spot: an ice blue that exists only in column 5 and the last beat of column 6; its rarity is the scare

layer_notes.1: Gradient radial oxblood to black breathing at about 6 seconds, with Abstract Field 'Smoke Storm' at low opacity underneath for candle smoke; in Cold Spot the gradient centre goes ice blue.
layer_notes.2: Geometry Pattern Maker is the wallpaper (Art Nouveau tile, red on black, slow rotate); Lines at 0 degrees are the venetian blinds (Giallo slat light, fuzz up on the drop); Checkered is the parquet floor for Black Gloves.
layer_notes.3: Metaballs: the ectoplasm and the drifting glass, three to five gold blobs on a slow orbit; Shaper is the single gold circle of the table and in Black Gloves a hard black polygon that cuts across the frame like a gloved hand.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope as candle flicker, random, warm, low intensity; Black Gloves swaps it for a hard white Stroboscope gated by the low band; Candles Out is Sine Wave as one guttering flame.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator in parchment, typed one letter at a time like the sitting record; Text Block for the three-line séance rules in The Ring.
layer_notes.6: Solid Color oxblood wash at low opacity for most columns; Cold Spot and the final four bars of Black Gloves swap to an ice-blue Gradient.
layer_notes.7: Golden Flicker Reel as a 1972 Technicolor print with gate weave and a hair in the gate; Static coarse and red only in Profondo Rosso.
layer_notes.8: Live FFT oscilloscope, same as every deck but tinted candle gold here.

moments: Hold the row-3 FIGURE pad under Glass Moves and roll the Mirror Quad bank knob up slowly: the drifting gold glass becomes four, then the wallpaper folds in on itself, and the room becomes a cathedral exactly when the bass drops.
Fire Scene Launch 5 (Cold Spot) on the breakdown so the whole wall goes ice blue for the first time all night, then tap the row-4 LIGHT pad once for a single candle flicker in the cold.

Black Gloves: mash the row-4 white strobe pad in eighths with the Shift RGB knob at three-quarters so the blinds split into red and cyan, then Up to Profondo Rosso and pull the Vignette knob fully closed on the last hit.

decks.name: Lamp Room
decks.world: The lamp room of a lighthouse on a Carpenter coast, 1979, 11:55 pm: a Fresnel lens the size of a man, a fog horn every thirty seconds, and a fog bank coming in that has a glow inside it. Light is the beam itself, a hard white wedge rotating through grey, and the moths that fly into it. The dread is slow and nautical, in the register of a light list and a notice to mariners, until the beam sweeps across the wall and something is standing in it. Bone white, fog grey, one sea teal, and anamorphic blue streaks on every point of light.

palette.why: fog grey-black: the bed is never black here, because fog has a floor
lens glass: pale grey-white for the Fresnel rings and the corridor, kept below white so the beam still wins
bone: the moths and the keeper's shapes, warm white against the cold grey
the beam; full white, hard edge, only on layer 4
sea teal, the one colour in the deck; a light-list entry reads like a tide table
deep teal wash for the sea and the glow in the fog; a flat red (#a31414) replaces it in Six Must Die only

layer_notes.1: Abstract Field 'Smoke Storm', grey, slow and full-frame: the fog, thick in Fog Bank, thinning to a Gradient sea-grey by Dawn Watch.
layer_notes.2: Tunnelines is the Fresnel lens seen from inside, slow rotation, lines in lens-glass grey; Line Scape is the sea as wireframe in Fog Bank and Dawn Watch; Lines at 90 degrees are rain for Fog Horn.
layer_notes.3: Metaballs small, many, bone-white, fast and jittery: the moths, more numerous as the energy rises; Shaper is the lamp itself, a hard white polygon that only appears in Lamp Lit and Beam Sweep.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope with the real light characteristic, two white flashes every 10 seconds, hard and short; Beam Sweep uses Sine Wave through SearchLight for the rotating wedge; Six Must Die is a full white Stroboscope gated by the low band.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator in sea teal set like a light-list line, fixed lower third; Fog Horn carries a thirty-second countdown as a Text Animator counter.
layer_notes.6: Gradient deep teal to black for the sea and the glow in the fog; Six Must Die swaps it to a flat red Solid Color.
layer_notes.7: Static very fine, white, slightly vertical: rain on the lens glass; Golden Flicker Reel low in Dawn Watch for the 16mm look.
layer_notes.8: Live FFT oscilloscope, white here, so it reads as the fog horn's own trace.

moments: Fire Scene Launch 3 (Lamp Lit) with the row-4 LIGHT pad held, and roll the SearchLight bank knob up: the hard white Shaper becomes a beam sweeping the whole wall, and every face in the room gets hit on each pass.

In Moths, tap the row-3 FIGURE pad on every kick to re-spawn the Metaballs swarm around the lamp with the Bloom knob at a quarter so each moth leaves a smear, then pull the knob to zero on the breakdown and the moths die.

Six Must Die: walk Up twice from FL 2 W 10S, mash the row-4 strobe pad in sixteenths and hit the Invert RGB button every fourth bar so the fog and the beam flash black, then Down to Dawn Watch and let the Trails knob bleed it out.

decks.name: Deep Field
decks.world: Christmas 1995: Hubble stares for ten days at an empty patch of sky near the Big Dipper, one twenty-eight-millionth of the whole, and three thousand galaxies come up out of the dark like a photograph in a tray. Light here accumulates; nothing flashes except a supernova, once. The wonder is patience and scale, the register is a FITS header and a Sagan sentence, and the colours are the false colours of the pipeline: dust gold, ionised violet, and the red of the oldest light. This is the come-down deck, the one you switch to when the room needs to breathe.

palette.why: the empty patch: as near to black as the LED wall can hold without going off
dust gold: spiral arms and dust lanes, the warm structure
ionised violet for the nebula blobs and the Einstein ring, the pipeline's false colour
star bloom: warm white, soft, through Bloom; the supernova is the only hard flash
FITS-header beige, small, like a plate annotation
deep magenta-violet wash that slides to red-shift crimson (#7a1f1f) by Oldest Light

layer_notes.1: Abstract Field 'Dot Dot Dot' at the lowest density and almost no motion: a handful of faint galaxies; Exposure pushes density up over the scene so the field fills in like a developing print.
layer_notes.2: Spiral, slow, two arms, dust gold, barely turning: the galaxy; Abstract Field 'Big Sweepers' for the dust lanes; Rings in Einstein Ring for the lensed arcs around a dark centre.
layer_notes.3: Metaballs, two or three, huge and soft, violet: the nebula; Shaper is the single lensed arc and, in Pale Blue Dot, one pale blue pixel-sized circle alone in the frame.
layer_notes.4: Gradient radial as a star's halo through Bloom, swelling with the smoothed low band; Supernova is a single Stroboscope flash with a 20-second refire, then nothing.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator in plate-annotation beige, small, bottom-left like a FITS header; Pale Blue Dot carries the one Sagan line and nothing else on screen.
layer_notes.6: Gradient diagonal violet to crimson, slow, becoming redder scene by scene as the deck red-shifts toward Oldest Light.
layer_notes.7: Static at the finest grain, very low: CCD read noise and the occasional hot pixel; never more than a whisper.
layer_notes.8: Live FFT oscilloscope, dim beige, thin, so it reads as the spectrum of the galaxy rather than a club meter.

moments: Exposure: hold the row-1 BED pad and push the Trails knob to three-quarters so every faint dot accumulates and never fades; the wall fills with galaxies over about a minute, then tap the pad again to clear the plate.

On the drop, walk Up from Einstein Ring into Supernova and slam the row-4 LIGHT pad for the single white flash, with the Infinite Zoom bank knob opened for two bars so the whole field falls inward, then shut.

Pale Blue Dot: kill every row but TEXT and FIGURE with the pads, leave the one pale pixel and the Sagan line on a black wall, and ride the Vignette knob so the dot is the only lit thing in the club for sixteen bars.

decks.name: Numbers Station
decks.world: A shortwave receiver at 3am somewhere between 4625 and 6959 kHz, 1976 to 2010: an interval tune on a music box, a woman's voice reading five-figure groups to nobody, and under it the buzzer that has not stopped since the Cold War. Light is phosphor amber on a band dial and the needle of an S-meter. The dread is bureaucratic and the wonder is that someone, somewhere, is writing the numbers down. It is the found-language deck: counting is the club's own grammar, and the text layer is the lead instrument.

palette.why: dial black, faintly warm: a radio in a dark room
phosphor amber, the P3 tube and the dial lamp; everything structural is this one orange
needle red-orange for the S-meter needle, the buzzer square and the jammer bars
dial-lamp white, warm, for the buzzer pulse and the carrier flash
lighter amber for the groups, so the numbers sit forward of the dial lines
burnt umber wash; in Jammer it goes to a sick olive (#3a3d12)

layer_notes.1: Static at low density, amber, with Lines horizontal and fine underneath: carrier hiss over a band dial; Jammer pushes the Static to full and the Lines to fast vertical bars.
layer_notes.2: Sine Wave is the carrier, one thick amber trace mirrored top and bottom, modulation on the low-mid band; Geometry Pattern Maker gives the one-time-pad grid in Five Groups; Checkered small and amber for the cipher page in Naimina.
layer_notes.3: Shaper as a single amber square that pulses on the buzzer; Rings for the interval signal's sweep in Interval; Spiral in Jammer as the spinning jammer wheel.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope at 25 flashes a minute, the real UVB-76 buzzer rate, amber-white; Achtung uses a Sine Wave flash on the attention call; Jammer is a full-frame Stroboscope gated by the high band.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator in amber, large, centred, one group at a time, retriggered by the pad on the beat: this is the deck's lead voice; Text Block for the three-line callsign sign-on.
layer_notes.6: Solid Color burnt umber at low opacity, flat; Jammer swaps to an olive Gradient.
layer_notes.7: Static coarse and slow (atmospherics), with Golden Flicker Reel off; Jammer adds a second Static at full for the barrage.
layer_notes.8: Live FFT oscilloscope in amber, bigger here, full-width lower third, because in a radio room the scope is the picture.

moments: Five Groups: tap the row-5 TEXT pad on every downbeat to fire the next five-figure group with the CRT knob at half so each group lands on scanlines, and let the row-2 Sine Wave carrier ride under it.

The Buzzer: hold the row-3 FIGURE pad so the amber square pulses at the buzzer rate while the row-4 strobe runs at the same 25 a minute, then open the Mirror Quad knob so one square becomes four and the four become a grid on the drop.

Naimina is the text drop: walk Up out of The Buzzer, tap the row-5 TEXT pad once so the single line stands alone on the dial, then Up again into Jammer and ride the Posterize knob up and the Vignette knob shut while the static barrage eats the voice.

effect_wishlist.role: phosphor persistence; the one effect that makes every deck look like a tube, and the accumulator for Exposure
lamp halo, candle, star bloom; the only pretty effect in the rack, kept low
scanlines and curvature on the text layer; the broadcast and terminal register
gives the wall a centre: the room edge, the dish aperture, the single lit dot
the lighthouse beam sweeping the wall; doubles as the séance torch
Giallo print misregistration; chromatic split on the drop
the symmetry drop: wallpaper, cathedral, cipher grid from any single figure on one button
the negative flash; the hit; momentary only, never left on
bone white: turns soft fields into hard Hammer cutouts
deep-field fall-in and the warp corridor for Tunnelines
composition-level white strobe for the last eight bars; white only, no colour
horizontal blue lens streaks on every point of light; Carpenter 2.35:1 on a club wall
three-strip Technicolor and Risograph flattening for the print look; eats the Jammer
stop the world on the drop and release it; the held frame before the beam returns

proposals.fft_philosophy: Sub and low (20 to 120 Hz) through a fast-attack, 400 ms release envelope drive only amplitude-type parameters: pulsar ridge height, Sine Wave amplitude, Metaballs size, Stroboscope gate and Bloom amount, so the kick is felt as a push, not a flash. Low-mid (120 to 500 Hz) through a 2-second envelope drives the slow structural things, the BED's density and the BODY's rotation speed, so the field breathes with the energy of the track rather than its transients; highs (6 to 16 kHz) drive GRAIN density, Static amount and Shift RGB offset, because hats are texture. Mids (vocals, leads) do nothing except gate the TEXT layer's opacity on a 300 ms hold, so words appear with phrases and never flicker. Nothing in the composition follows the FFT 1:1 without an envelope or a gate, except layer 8, the scope, which is the one honest karaoke element and is there so the rest can afford to be musical. Never reactive: text position, size and content; any hue or palette value; the BED's hue and position; Line Scape and Tunnelines camera moves; and the master output level.
proposals.wildcard_rationale: A numbers station is where the other two themes already overlap: it is the radio sky of the astronomer heard from a kitchen table, and it is the séance's voice in the static made bureaucratic. It is the performer's own register, found language, period broadcast, a counting cadence that is literally the club's count-in, and it gives the TEXT layer a deck where it is the lead instrument instead of the caption. Its phosphor-amber palette is the only warm-monochrome world in the pack, so switching to it from the white Lamp Room or the violet Deep Field is a hard tonal drop, and its energy arc (hiss, tune, call-up, groups, buzzer, voice, jamming, sign-off) is an eight-scene set in miniature.

proposals.tagline: Five rooms where someone is listening to the dark, and the dark, occasionally, replies.

decks.name: Hydrogen Line
decks.world: A radio telescope at night, tuned to 1420 MHz, with a chart recorder scratching the sky onto paper. The light is a long exposure: not black but the grey of sensor bias, with one white pen-trace and, far away, the red of hydrogen-alpha. The wonder is that the universe answers in scruff: a quarter-inch of ink in 1967, seventy-two seconds in 1977, three thousand galaxies in eleven days. Period register is the listening post, not the launch pad: Cambridge chart paper, Big Ear printouts, Voyager's record sleeve.

palette.why: Not pure black: the dark of a long exposure, with a faint blue sensor bias so Add-blend layers have something to sit on.
The CP1919 ridgelines and all chart annotations; warm white, never pure, so Bloom does not clip it to nothing.
656 nm emission red, reserved for AURA and the one Wow Signal word; the only red in the deck so it reads as an event.
The blue of young galaxies in the Hubble frame; FIGURE metaballs and the Red Shift gradient start here before sliding warm.
The one warm thing in the control room; LIGHT only, at low opacity, so the dish feels staffed.
Chart-paper margin grey for low-urgency telemetry text and the BED star-noise; keeps most of the deck below the eye's attention.

layer_notes.1: Abstract Field, Dot Dot Dot preset, in margin grey at 12%: a sparse drifting star-noise floor that breathes very slowly with the sub band; in Dark Run it is the only thing on.
layer_notes.2: React Pulsar in chart-paper white on void, the CP1919 stacked ridgelines as the deck's spine; swaps to Lines (horizontal rules, slight fuzz) in Dark Run and Arecibo so the paper is there before the signal.
layer_notes.3: Metaballs as galaxy cores in Deep Field, three to five, slow; Rings as the dish's beam pattern in Scruff and Wow; Spiral, very slow, in Red Shift sliding from blue to hydrogen red via AURA.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope at one flash per two bars as the dish beacon, dial-lamp amber; in Wow Signal a single Gradient radial hit on the bar; Sine Wave mirrored as the bright pen stroke in CP 1919.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator, chart-recorder annotations in margin grey, small, bottom third; Wow Signal is the only column where TEXT is hydrogen red and full width.
layer_notes.6: Solid Color hydrogen alpha, Add, 0% in Dark Run rising to 8% by Red Shift; Gradient linear deep-field blue to void in Deep Field.
layer_notes.7: Static, fine, 6%, as chart-paper tooth; no Golden Flicker Reel in this deck, it is the clean deck.
layer_notes.8: The FFT Sine Wave trace, same in every deck; here it reads as the chart pen, chart-paper white, one line high at the bottom edge.

moments: Hold the BODY pad in the Scruff column (row 2, column 2) and roll the bank-A dry/wet knob up slowly: the ridgelines spread into Bloom and the paper seems to breathe with the bass; roll it back and the scruff is just ink again.

Scene Launch 4 fires Wow Signal: TEXT slams 6EQUJ5 in red while LIGHT flashes once on the bar; tap the Freeze effect button on the same beat and hold the burst for exactly seventy-two seconds if the room can take it.
Walk Up from Deep Field to Golden Record with the bank-B Delay RGB knob at a third: the metaball galaxies split into colour ghosts, and the Voyager lines arrive one per press of the row-5 TEXT pad.

decks.name: Loss Of Signal
decks.world: Mission Control's voice loop at the moment the spacecraft goes behind the Moon: LOS, forty-five minutes of dead air, and the whistling the Apollo 10 crew heard on the far side and nearly did not report. The room is console grey, green phosphor and one amber tally lamp; everything else is the dark the carrier left behind. The dread is that the loop keeps counting into silence and the voice that eventually answers may not be on the roster. Period register is 1969 Houston: teletype paper, capcom cadence, hiss at 2.2 kHz.

palette.why: The Eagle-room console paint; BED checker and the SCOPE frame, so the deck feels like furniture, not space.
P39 monitor green, the only living colour; TEXT and BODY, and it must stay the same green in every column so the room is one room.
The single tally lamp; LIGHT only, flashing on the bar, the room's heartbeat.
Near-black with a blue cast for the Dead Air column, where the BED is this and nothing else.
A colour that does not belong in Houston; AURA only, zero until LOS, rising in Whistling, the visual sign that something else is on the loop.
Paper white for timestamps and the Splashdown newsreel; the colour of the transcript, used sparingly.

layer_notes.1: Checkered at very large scale, console grey on dead-air black, 4% contrast, the room's grid; in Dead Air it collapses to Solid Color dead-air and the faintest Static.
layer_notes.2: Lines, horizontal, zero rotation, fuzz rising with low-mids: the voice-loop trace in phosphor green; in Whistling it becomes Tunnelines, the far side as a corridor you are being pulled down.
layer_notes.3: Shaper, a single thin circle outline (the lunar limb) drifting edge to edge across the whole scene set, so the Moon crosses the room over eight columns; in Whistling a Sine Wave with heavy modulation and mirror.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope, tally amber, one flash per bar, square; Gradient radial amber at 10% in Acquisition as the room's lights come back.
layer_notes.5: Text Animator in phosphor green, loop chatter in capcom register, left-justified like a transcript; in Whistling the only column where the text is far-side violet.
layer_notes.6: Solid Color far-side violet, Add, 0% from Go For TLI to LOS In Ten, 12% in Whistling, back to 0% at Acquisition.
layer_notes.7: Static, coarse, stepped to 2 fps: the 2.2 kHz hiss; Golden Flicker Reel only in Splashdown, the newsreel at the end.
layer_notes.8: The FFT trace, here read as the downlink carrier; it is the one thing still moving in Dead Air.

moments: Scene Launch 3 then Scene Launch 4 in a row: LOS In Ten counts down on TEXT, then Dead Air kills every layer except BED and SCOPE; let the room hear the silence for a full phrase before you touch a pad.

In Whistling, hold the FIGURE pad (row 3) and turn the bank-B dry/wet knob up: Tunnel and WarpSpeed pull the corridor inward while the violet aura climbs with it; release the pad and the corridor snaps back to the console.

On Alarm 1202, hit the Strobe effect button on the downbeat and ride the bank-C knob: Shift Glitch tears the phosphor text; Scene Launch 5 is Whistling, so walk Up twice to Acquisition and it resets clean.

decks.name: The Sitters
decks.world: A Victorian parlour seance by one candle, run to a strict protocol: lamp down, hands joined, knock once for yes, never break the circle. The light is a single flame that a moth keeps crossing, and everything it does not reach is the brown of a daguerreotype. The dread is procedural: the table tilts on schedule, the trumpet lifts, and the wax cylinder plays back a name nobody gave it. Period register is 1872 Hackney with a 1971 overdub: Raudive's Class A voices under the hiss.

palette.why: Warm black, the colour of a room with the lamp down; the BED's far edge and the Multiply floor.
The only light source; LIGHT and the BED's radial centre, gutters on onsets.
Cold muslin grey-white for FIGURE metaballs, the one cool thing in a warm room, so it reads as not belonging.
Sepia for the AURA Multiply and the BODY wallpaper; it makes everything look already photographed.
Wing-scale grey-brown for the Trails and the moth's orbit; dull on purpose.
Dried-blood red used only in the Class A column for the voice that answers; everywhere else TEXT is ectoplasm white.

layer_notes.1: Gradient radial, candle to parlour black, pulled off-centre to the upper left, breathing with the sub band; it is the room and in Lights Down it is all there is.
layer_notes.2: Geometry Pattern Maker at 6% as the parlour wallpaper, a tiled damask you never quite see; in The Table it swaps to Lines, vertical, tilting slowly left as the table does.
layer_notes.3: Metaballs, two or three, soft, slow, in ectoplasm white: the muslin; in Moth To Lamp a single Shaper point orbiting the candle with Trails; in Trumpet Lifts a Shaper cone rising over four bars.
layer_notes.4: Stroboscope at an irregular slow rate with a flame-coloured gradient, the candle gutter; Golden Flicker Reel through a radial Mask in Lights Down, the lamp dying.
layer_notes.5: Text Block in the medium's protocol voice, ectoplasm white, centred, one or two short lines; Class A is the only column using Text Animator letter by letter, in class A red.
layer_notes.6: Solid Color daguerreotype, Multiply, 30%; drops to a cold grey Screen at 10% in Class A and Break Circle.
layer_notes.7: Static, fine, as cylinder hiss at 8%; Golden Flicker Reel sprocket damage added in Break Circle only.
layer_notes.8: The FFT trace, here read as the EVP recorder's needle, in moth dust, almost not there.

moments: Fire Scene Launch 1 (Lights Down) and leave only BED and SCOPE up for a full minute; then press the row-4 LIGHT pad in Knock Once exactly on a kick so the candle gutters as the knock.
In Moth To Lamp, hold the FIGURE pad (row 3) and roll the bank-A knob up: Trails lengthens the moth's orbit until it is a ring of dust around the flame; back the knob off and it dies in two bars.
Walk Up to Class A and tap the Invert RGB button for exactly one beat: the parlour goes negative, the red line of the voice shows through, and the sepia returns when you let go.

decks.name: Hour Of Saturn
decks.world: A grimoire read under Giallo light: the circle drawn in chalk, the planetary hour struck, the lamp swapped for a red gel and then a blue one, the way a corridor in Suspiria or a Hammer crypt is lit from the wrong side. The body of the world is geometry, seals, heptagons and contracting rings, which assembles and then breaks. The dread is formal: the ritual is a recipe and the recipe is working. Period register is the Key of Solomon by way of a 1977 Rome print lab, with a Carpenter pulse underneath.

palette.why: Argento red, the first gel; LIGHT and AURA only, never on text, so the words stay chalk.
The second gel, the counter-light from the other side of the room; alternates with red on the bar.
The circle and the text, slightly warm so it reads as chalk on stone, not white on screen.
Dead-flat warm black so the gels have nothing to reflect off except the geometry.
Bronze gone green for the FIGURE seal; the one colour neither gel can produce, so the seal always looks older than the light.
The warm neutral for the SCOPE and secondary text; it keeps the deck from being only red, blue and white.

layer_notes.1: Solid Color crypt black with a Gradient linear red-to-blue at 10% that rotates once every two minutes: the two gels crossing on the back wall.
layer_notes.2: Geometry Pattern Maker in chalk at 25%, the circle's tiled sigils, slowly scaling; in Conjuration it swaps to Rings, tight and many, contracting over eight bars.
layer_notes.3: Shaper heptagon, outline only, verdigris, rotating one turn per minute: the seal; in The Lamp Goes it shrinks to a single verdigris point and stays.
layer_notes.4: Gradient radial, hard-edged, gel red, placed off-centre like a lamp from the wrong side; Stroboscope in gel blue on the bar in Blue Gel; both lamps at once in Conjuration.
layer_notes.5: Text Block in chalk, the planetary-hour register, two short lines maximum, set high; Conjuration uses Text Animator letter by letter in bone.
layer_notes.6: Solid Color gel red, Multiply, 35% in Red Gel; gel blue, Screen, 25% in Blue Gel; both stacked in Conjuration; off in Chalk Circle and Licence To Go.
layer_notes.7: Golden Flicker Reel as the print's flicker at 15% throughout; Static, coarse, added only in Hour Struck as the hour sounds.
layer_notes.8: The FFT trace in bone, here read as the pulse of the synth; the only element that is allowed to look like music.

moments: Scene Launch 4 then 5 on alternate bars (Red Gel, Blue Gel): the lamp swaps sides on the downbeat; bring the bank-D knob to a quarter so Kaleidoscope multiplies the chalk seal with the second gel and no further.

In Conjuration, hold the BODY pad (row 2) and the FIGURE pad (row 3) together and push the bank-A knob to full: Rings contract into the heptagon under Bloom until the frame whites out; drop the knob and the circle is empty.

The Lamp Goes: walk Up once from Conjuration, then release the row-4 LIGHT pad on a snare so only the verdigris point and the TEXT remain; walk Up again to Licence To Go and the text reads the dismissal.

decks.name: German Bight
decks.world: The 0048 shipping forecast: a voice reading sea areas into the dark, after Sailing By, for people who may or may not be out there. It is the North Sea at night as a wireframe swell with one lighthouse sweep and a grey that is almost blue. The wonder is liturgical: Viking, North Utsire, Forties, a low losing its identity, and the gale warnings carry real dread without a single horror cue. Period register is BBC Radio 4 long wave at 198 kHz and a Met Office card read in a flat voice.

palette.why: Sea-at-night black with a blue cast; the BED's far horizon and the AURA's outer edge.
The wireframe sea and the barometer trace; a grey that is nearly blue, never cold enough to be space.
The lamp; LIGHT only, as a narrow rotating gradient, the one warm thing for thirty miles.
The Met Office card; all TEXT, slightly yellowed like paper read under a desk lamp.
Gale warnings only; a red that reads storm cone, not blood, used on AURA at 6% and on one word.
The one screen on the bridge; the SCOPE trace and the Radar effect sweep, the only green in the deck.

layer_notes.1: Line Scape, the 3D wireframe sea in swell grey, camera low, amplitude on the sub band, speed fixed so the swell never hurries; it is the deck's whole floor.
layer_notes.2: Sine Wave, mirrored, very low frequency: the swell line and barometer trace in one; in Gale Warnings its amplitude and fuzz climb with low-mids and the line thickens.
layer_notes.3: Rings, slow expand, one new ring every four bars: the pulse from the lighthouse; in Dogger Fisher a Shaper square outline drifts across, the buoy, the card.
layer_notes.4: Gradient linear, lighthouse-coloured, narrow, rotating once per sixteen bars: the sweep; Radar effect on this layer in German Bight so it reads as the bridge screen.
layer_notes.5: Text Block in card white, two short lines, area then forecast, set low and left like a card on a desk; Gale Warnings is the only column with one word in gale red.
layer_notes.6: Gradient radial, long wave to swell grey, 15%, centred on the horizon; gale red Add at 6% in Gale Warnings and Lundy Fastnet only.
layer_notes.7: Static, fine, as long-wave hiss at 10%; Lines vertical and fuzzed at 5% as rain later, in Dogger Fisher and Rockall Malin.
layer_notes.8: The FFT trace in bridge radar green, here read as the barograph: the only element that admits there is music playing.

moments: Scene Launch 1 (Sailing By) with every effect button off and the bank-A knob at zero; bring in the row-4 LIGHT pad on the second bar and let the lighthouse sweep be the only motion for as long as you dare.

On Gale Warnings, hold the BODY pad (row 2) and push the bank-B knob: Wave Warp and Ripples stack on the swell line and the red aura rises; press the row-5 TEXT pad in column 2 on the hit so SEVERE GALE 9 lands with it.
Walk Up through the sea areas one column per phrase of the music; at Fair Isle press the row-5 TEXT pad on the last beat so LOSING ITS IDENTITY is the final line of the set.

effect_wishlist.role: The one glow: phosphor, candle and gel alike; bank A, the knob the performer lives on.
Persistence: the moth's orbit, the pulsar's afterimage, the sweep's tail; bank A.
The colour ghost; splits galaxies and gels into misregistered copies; bank B, never above a third.
The far-side corridor; pulls FIGURE inward in Whistling and Conjuration; bank B.
Paired with Tunnel for the Whistling column only; the one moment the instrument is allowed to accelerate; bank B.
The swell: bends the Sine Wave body in Gale Warnings and the trumpet in The Sitters; bank B.
Table-tilt and sea-state; slow and large, on BED only; bank B.
Multiplies the chalk seal under the second gel; bank D, capped at four segments so it never becomes a screensaver.
Console curvature and scanline on the two space decks at 20%; bank C, left on.
Every room is dark at its edges; bank C, permanently around 40%, the deck's frame.
The bridge screen in German Bight and the dish beam in Hydrogen Line; bank C.
Alarm 1202 and the Class A tear; momentary button, never on a knob above 30%.
The gel swap and the tally lamp; button only, rate-limited to once per bar by hand.
The negative frame where the voice shows; one-beat tap, then release, never held.

proposals.fft_philosophy: Sub and low bass (below about 120 Hz) own only slow continuous parameters - BED amplitude, Line Scape swell, gradient breath, metaball size - with heavy smoothing, so a kick reads as a tide and never as a jump. Low-mids (120 to 600 Hz) drive BODY density, line fuzz and FIGURE rotation speed; highs (above 4 kHz) are allowed only onto GRAIN opacity and the SCOPE trace, so hi-hats become hiss and nothing else. Onsets are triggers, not levels: one Stroboscope flash, one candle gutter, one glitch frame, quantised to the beat and rate-limited to once per bar. TEXT never reacts - not position, not scale, not opacity - because words arrive by hand on the pad, and a word that bounces is karaoke. Hue, blend mode and AURA colour never react either: colour is a decision the performer makes with a scene, and the music is only permitted to change how much light is in the room, never what colour the room is.
proposals.wildcard_rationale: Space and Halloween are both about receiving voices from where no one should be: the pulsar, the far side of the Moon, the parlour, the circle. The shipping forecast is the broadcast that goes the other way, a voice sent into the dark at 0048 on the assumption that someone is out there, which makes it the third kind of listening post and completes the set. It is also the most Radiophonic text in English: a liturgy made of place-names and numbers read in a flat BBC register, which is exactly the EarthSearch and Lexicon grammar this performer already plays. As the fifth deck it is the come-down: after the ritual peaks in Hour Of Saturn, the set ends on the North Sea near dawn with a low losing its identity, and its gale warnings carry real dread without a single horror cue.
